patch.value: Measure agent task cost baselines for extension authors

Reproducible consumer-example baselines for orientation, targeted-read and resume scenarios. Measures tool calls, delivered bytes and elapsed work. Not model performance, not external capture accounting, and not native operation benchmarks.

Every baseline declares corpus/version and expected answer; repeated runs report distributions; byte/4 estimates are labeled estimates; a deliberate extra full-list call worsens the measured call/byte budget.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text:
Overlap check (re-run against the pinned SDK 2026.10.23 and sibling package READMEs before design):

- pm-cli ships an internal release ratchet (docs/agent-task-token-baseline.json plus the agent-task token gate). It replays fixed CLI transcripts and compares ceil(bytes/4) estimates for core protocols. That gate is a core release claim, not a consumer example extension authors can run against their own tracker.
- pm-observer measures external producer captures (transcript tokens, attribution, continuity). It does not measure SDK tool-call and delivered-byte budgets for fixed orientation, targeted-read and resume scenarios.
- pm-rust benchmarks native workspace operations. It is not a TypeScript consumer example.

This item is a reproducible pm-starter example for extension authors. It declares corpus/version and an expected answer, reports distributions over repeated runs, labels byte/4 figures as estimates, and shows that one extra full-list call worsens the measured call and byte budget. It does not claim model performance.

Design: host-injected SDK only (context orient intent, certified list, get, producer cursors, schemaList roles, workspace transactions). No argv/which/symlink SDK resolution.
